{{Short description|Japanese mathematician (1947–2022)}}
{{Nihongo|'''Takao Nishizeki'''|西関 隆夫|Nishizeki Takao|1947 – 30 January 2022<ref>{{citation|url=http://list.dia.uniroma3.it/pipermail/gdnet/2022/000132.html|title=Takao Nishizeki|work=GDNET|first=Yoshio|last=Okamoto|date=1 February 2022}}</ref>}} was a Japanese mathematician and computer scientist who specialized in [[graph algorithm]]s and [[graph drawing]].

==Education and career==
Nishizeki was born in 1947 in [[Fukushima, Fukushima|Fukushima]], and was a student at [[Tohoku University]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1969, a master's in 1971, and a doctorate in 1974. He continued at Tohoku as a faculty member, and became a full professor there in 1988.<ref>[http://www.ecei.tohoku.ac.jp/alg/nishizeki/sub/e/bio.html Biography], Tohoku University, retrieved 2015-03-19.</ref> He was the Dean of the Graduate School of Information Sciences, Tohoku University, from April 2008 to March 2010. He retired in 2010, becoming a professor emeritus at Tohoku University, but continued teaching as a professor at [[Kwansei Gakuin University]] until March 2015.<ref>[http://researchers.kwansei.ac.jp/view?l=en&u=46077 Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215643/http://researchers.kwansei.ac.jp/view?l=en&u=46077 |date=2016-03-03 }}, Kwansei Gakuin University, retrieved 2015-03-19.</ref> He was an Auditor of Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology from April 2016 to October 2018.

==Contributions==
Nishizeki made significant contributions to algorithms for [[series–parallel graph]]s,{{sfnp|Takamizawa|Nishizeki|Saito|1982}} finding [[clique (graph theory)|cliques]] in [[sparse graph]]s,{{sfnp|Chiba|Nishizeki|1985}} [[planarity testing]]{{sfnp|Chiba|Nishizeki|Abe|Ozawa|1985}} and the secret sharing with any access structure. He is the co-author of two books on [[planar graph]]s and [[graph drawing]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Nishizeki|Chiba|1988}}; {{harvtxt|Nishizeki|Rahman|2004}}.</ref>

In 1990, Nishizeki founded the annual [[International Symposium on Algorithms and Computation]] (ISAAC).<ref name="isaac"/>

==Awards and honors==
At the 18th ISAAC symposium, in 2007, a workshop was held to celebrate his 60th birthday.<ref name="isaac">[http://denseoutliers.blogspot.com/2007/12/isaac-day-1.html ISAAC Day 1], Joachim Gudmundsson, dense outliers, December 21, 2007, retrieved 2015-03-19.</ref>

In 1996, he became a [[IEEE Fellow|life fellow of the IEEE]] "for contributions to graph algorithms with applications to physical design of electronic systems."<ref>[http://www.ieee-jp.org/section/tokyo/fellow/winner/fellow95.htm 1995 New Fellows], IEEE Japan Section, retrieved 2015-03-19.</ref>
In 1996 he was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] "for contributions to the design and analysis of efficient algorithms for planar graphs, network flows and VLSI routing".<ref>[[List of Fellows of the Association for Computing Machinery|ACM Fellow]] [http://awards.acm.org/award_winners/nishizeki_3042207.cfm award citation], retrieved 2015-03-19.</ref>
Nishizeki was also a foreign fellow of the [[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]];<ref>[http://www.bas.org.bd/fellowship/list-of-fellows-/userprofile/nishizeki.html Member profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923182539/http://www.bas.org.bd/fellowship/list-of-fellows-/userprofile/nishizeki.html |date=2015-09-23 }}, Bangladesh Academy of Sciences, retrieved 2015-03-20.</ref> one of his students and frequent co-authors, [[Saidur Rahman (professor, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology)|Md. Saidur Rahman]], is from Bangladesh.
